review_scope: Independent Pearson kernel numerical recheck only

WR-07.mechanism_reviewed: Power-of-two scaling bounds values, reference-observation offsets preserve small spreads at a common large offset, a second spread scaling and unit-vector normalization avoid raw squared moments. Public Pearson uses bounded normalized dot product; Spearman is a separate retained rank path.
WR-07.independent_oracle: Exact binary64 Fraction raw moments n*sum(x*y)-sum(x)*sum(y), n*sum(x*x)-sum(x)^2 and n*sum(y*y)-sum(y)^2; 160-significant-digit Decimal square root/division. No developer test or fixture imported.
actual_coverage: Original small/normal/large independently scaled positive and negative pair reproductions
Non-perfect/nonlinear covariance with non-equally-spaced offsets and ties
Smallest subnormal, minimum normal and maximum finite float64 values
Positive/negative large shared offsets with ULP-sized variation and row permutations
Mixed dynamic range and almost orthogonal/zero covariance
720 deterministically seeded random cases across wide exponents, shared offsets and nearly perfect pairs
16 pairwise absolute-Pearson matrix subcases with common-sample missingness

tolerance.basis: 128 times binary64 epsilon for tested vectors up to 32 observations; absolute, not relative, assessment near zero
tolerance.worst_case: Two-point negative correlation in deterministic random-wide case1: exact -1 versus computed -0.9999999999999998; ordinary last-bit rounding, not a defect

unverified: Exhaustive correctness over every possible finite vector or unlimited sample count
Relative accuracy of correlations whose true magnitude is below binary64 absolute rounding
Real financial data, factor validity or market/portfolio performance
